title: Targeted comparison against a simpler configuration
labels: DETERMINISTIC FIXTURE PROVIDER — scripted workers in real processes; no model was run
SYNTHETIC DATA — every request, team, dataset and value is invented
INJECTED DEFECTS — in about half of the episodes one worker's first attempt carries a defect its own tests do not catch

The defect rate is an assumption of this testbed. The comparison shows what the verification swarm catches when such defects occur, and what it costs; it does not show how often they occur in real work.

steps.claim: The simpler configuration is a coordination-level candidate with its own version
steps.observed: coordination v1 → candidate: Sets independent_verification to false: no verification swarm is formed and the integrated result is accepted on delivery's own combined tests.

steps.claim: Both configurations run the same seeded missions end to end
steps.observed: 8 complete fixture missions per configuration from held-out set missions-A; a defect is injected into a first attempt in about half of them

steps.claim: The simpler configuration really is cheaper and faster
steps.observed: worker invocations per mission 12.875 → 10; completion 3978 ms → 2868 ms

steps.claim: What it gives up is measured by an oracle, not assumed
steps.observed: defects reaching an accepted result per mission 0 → 0.625; truly correct missions 1 → 0.375 (difference -0.625, 95% interval -0.875 to -0.25)

steps.claim: The decision follows the frozen rule
steps.observed: reject: Rejected: no more defects escape failed. Acceptance criteria that fail on results the mission accepted: candidate 5, incumbent 0, across 8 episodes.
